residuals.title: Launch receipt effective comes from the installed CLI, never copied from requested
Launch receipt effective for Cursor also comes from the installed CLI, not the catalog-only clone
residuals.note: Round-3 review finding: CURSOR_SESSION_OPTION_CATALOG sets supportsWorkerLaunchPreferences: true, but PROBEABLE_LAUNCH_AGENTS excluded cursor, so a cursor launch fell to the bottom catalog-only branch -- effective: {...selection}, honestly labelled source: 'catalog' but never checked against the installed CLI. At upstream this whole probe apparatus does not exist yet, so every agent's receipt is the unconditional clone; the reproduce regex pins the same 'source': 'catalog' (never 'probe') diff line the I entry's fix already closed for claude/codex.

residuals.title: source: 'probe' requires the discovery answer's own catalogOrigin; a failed probe is not memoised past its own call
residuals.note: Round-4 review finding, Odin-introduced (I4a): verifyAgentLaunchSelection labelled the outcome source: 'probe' on result.success alone, but discoverCommitMessageModelsLocal also returns success: true, catalogOrigin: 'spec' when the installed CLI exits 0 with no parseable model list and finalizeModelDiscoveryOutput falls back to the static catalog -- that fallback earned the same 'probe' label as a real live-CLI answer. Fixed by threading catalogOrigin through AgentLaunchVerification and labelling 'catalog' unless catalogOrigin === 'probe'. (I4b, same commit): probeAgentModelsOnce memoised the discover() promise for the process lifetime including failures, keyed by (executor, agentId), so one transient miss pinned every later worker-start for that agent to 'unverified' forever; fixed by evicting the cache entry on any failed outcome so the next launch re-probes. At upstream 539d4d1f32b4 resolveWorkerLaunchPreferences is synchronous (I3's own comment: no probe exists at all) so `await`ing its plain return object is a no-op; the I4a test's own `.resolves` matcher throws 'You must provide a Promise' first (an infrastructure mismatch, not used as the reproduction, matching the I3 precedent), but the I4b test reaches a real, meaningful assertion: `first.receipt.source` is `undefined` there (no `source` field exists on the synchronous receipt at all) where this test expects `'unverified'` -- pinned as the reproduce regex.

residuals.title: Worker liveness: an empty or non-enumerating host answer is unverifiable, never exited
classifyTerminalProcessInspectionFailure gives terminal_handle_stale/terminal_exited/no_connected_pty/a PTY-not-found message their own reasons instead of the host-proven terminal_gone
residuals.note: docs/reference/ssh-execution-boundary.md's own 'terminal_gone is overloaded' paragraph names this exact bug: classifyTerminalProcessInspectionFailure (shared/terminal-process-inspection.ts:83-95) bucketed a client-side registry miss (stale handle, exited entry, no connected pty, a 'PTY "<id>" not found' message) under the same 'terminal_gone' string as the host's own relay-side tombstone claim. This function and its bucketing are byte-identical at upstream 539d4d1f32b4 (verified by diff) -- a genuine inherited Orca residual, not Odin-introduced -- so it is recorded in the existing hash-cited shape once the fix commit exists.

closedByConstruction.title: Relay tombstone applies the same proof gate (record-torn-down is not a death)
closedByConstruction.note: Closed by construction, not mechanically reproduced: upstream src/relay/pty-handler.ts:2412 hard-codes code: 0 in reapExitedPty even for evidence 'record-torn-down' (its own docblock at :2395-2402 says that is not a death), and :2632-2656 publishes verdict 'exited' from it. Odin routes the code through resolveRetiredPtyIncarnationCode (UNVERIFIED_PROCESS_EXIT_CODE unless the evidence is a proven exit) and the consumer applies the same isProvenProcessExit gate as the daemon (A). The race has no deterministic harness in the relay test surface, so its test pins the extracted mapping rather than reproducing the upstream path.

closedByConstruction.title: A structured worker's own host-owned unverifiable is never treated as absent on release
closedByConstruction.note: Closed by construction, not mechanically reproduced: worker-release-completion.ts's missing/unattached branch was widened under O2 to also match `observation.status === 'unverifiable' && observation.terminal === null`, gated on `terminal === null` rather than on which observer produced the observation. observeStructuredWorker also reports `terminal: null` for its own legitimate host-owned `unverifiable` (host not installed, no durable record, non-native lease, no attached child), so a structured worker in that state joined the same branch as an absent PTY -- in recovery mode this reaches inspectTerminalProcessIncarnationLiveness, a check built for PTY incarnations, and could settle the release from its answer as if the worker were absent. Fixed by tagging inspectWorkerTerminal's return with an explicit `kind: 'pty' | 'structured'` and gating the clause on `kind === 'pty'` instead of `terminal === null`. At upstream 539d4d1f32b4 this clause is `observation.status === 'missing' || observation.status === 'unattached'` with no `unverifiable` case at all -- the O2 fix that introduced the wider clause postdates this fork, so the bug (and the fix) exist only inside Odin's own code; running this test's mocks against upstream's narrower clause passes there too, for an unrelated reason (upstream never considers `unverifiable` in this branch to begin with), so it is not usable as an upstream reproduction. odin/proofs/O3a.before.txt/.after.txt instead pin the test failing against Odin's own pre-fix clause (`observation.terminal === null`) and passing against the fix (`observation.kind === 'pty'`).
